confirmed: Source.version correctly identifies an abstract-only Crossref record for the 2024 SSRN working paper, not a full-text reading. I independently read the complete Crossref abstract; retrieval.json marks c152 not_obtained, SSRN returned HTTP 403, and OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar returned null abstracts and only the SSRN DOI as an access location (Crossref API https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2139/ssrn.4751779; https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4751779; https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4751779; https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/DOI:10.2139/ssrn.4751779?fields=title,authors,year,abstract,openAccessPdf,url,externalIds).

The title and author order match Crossref: How AI Outperforms Humans at Creative Idea Generation; Noah Castelo, Zsolt Katona, Peiyao Li, Miklos Sarvary; posted-content dated 2024 (Crossref metadata, title, author, type, and posted fields at https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2139/ssrn.4751779).

The abstract describes product ideas generated by GPT4 compared with ideas from laypeople and financially incentivized creative professionals, plus GPT4 rewrites compared with original human ideas; ai_vs_human is supported for these described comparisons (Crossref abstract, sentences beginning This paper, We first demonstrate, and Finally).

All reported strings and both participants.quote strings match the Crossref abstract verbatim. S1-O1 is supported by the sentence beginning We first demonstrate; S1-O2 and S1-O3 by We find; S2-O1 by Finally (Crossref abstract).

The one_line_finding accurately summarizes the abstract: GPT4 ideas are rated more creative, GPT4 outperforms humans in creative form and substance, and GPT4 rewrites are rated significantly more creative, with the rewrite improvement explained by form (Crossref abstract, sentences beginning We first demonstrate, We find, and Finally).

Creative form is unusual or unique descriptive language; creative substance concerns novelty of the idea itself. The abstract identifies a text-analysis methodology but provides no implementation details (Crossref abstract, sentences beginning We then propose and We develop).

The null people counts, arm counts, and n_units are appropriate: the complete abstract gives no numbers of people, ideas, or ratings, no randomized-versus-analyzed counts, and no effect estimates, intervals, or exact test statistics. Whether any study analyzed fewer than 50 people cannot be determined (Crossref abstract, entire text).

No randomized people study is documented in the accessible abstract; has_randomized_people_study = false here means none identified, not a verified absence from the unavailable full paper. The number of actual studies, independent samples, and allocation procedures cannot be established from the two comparisons described (Crossref abstract, entire text).

The source describes original empirical comparisons, not a synthesis; there are no pooled estimates or study-count claims to verify, and the form appropriately leaves synthesis counts null and pooled empty (Crossref abstract, entire text).
summary: The complete Crossref abstract supports the reported findings and the AI-versus-human comparisons, but no full text was accessible and no randomized people study could be established. Five corrections address unsupported claims about human AI use, definitive exclusion from core eligibility, rater identity, and analysis units, plus the abstract's explicit evidence that creativity was scored on output.
